text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Monthly inflation in Bulgaria in December was 21 percent and the annual inflation in 1996 was 292 percent, National Statistics Institute preliminary figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's Trade ministry lifted customs duties on the imports of 6,000 tonnes of natural gas for domestic consumption from January 1 to March 31.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet raised electricity and coal prices by 43 percent, effective from January 1.
-- Slovenia will lift customs duties on 55 percent of industrial imports from Bulgaria under a bilateral free trade agreement effective from January 1.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet and the central bank are considering restructuring of short term domestic debt into long term government bonds in a bid to avoid a default on domestic debt payments. @
Bulgaria's internal debt rose to 700-800 billion levs in December with some 25 percent of the total being a long term debt with maturity between two and 10 years.
-- Bulgaria'a main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) said it expected some 70,000 people to join a protest rally in Sofia today with demands for early parliamentary elections.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet is expected to discuss today the 1997 draft budget in which an annual inflation of 72 percent and an average exchange rate of 500 levs per dollar were projected. @
-- Bulgaria's Agriculture ministry is expected to offer 70 companies for privatisation this year, a senior ministry official said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
